catalyst_text: Positive Phase 3 topline results planning BLA submission
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial in Acute Myeloid Leukemia maintenance, meeting the primary endpoint of overall survival. The study showed a 41% reduction in risk of death versus best available treatment with median overall survival of 24.0 months vs 14.7 months and a hazard ratio of 0.59 (p=0.035). The population included patients in second or later remission ineligible for allogeneic transplant.
catalyst_text_evidence: SELLAS Life Sciences Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: SLS) (“SELLAS” or the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company focused on the development of novel therapies for a broad range of cancer indications, today announced positive topline results from the pivotal randomized Phase 3 REGAL trial evaluating galinpepimut-S (GPS), an immunotherapeutic cancer vaccine, in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The REGAL trial met its primary endpoint of overall survival (OS), with GPS demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in OS compared with investigator’s choice of best available treatment (BAT). In the trial, GPS showed a 41% reduction in the risk of death (hazard ratio of 0.59) and a two-sided p=0.035 with a median OS of 24.0 months among GPS-treated patients versus 14.7 months with BAT. The pivotal trial evaluated GPS as maintenance monotherapy in patients who achieved a second or later complete remission (CR2 or later) or complete remission with insufficient platelet recovery (CRp2 or later) following second- or later-line salvage therapy and who were ineligible for, or unable to undergo, allogeneic stem cell transplantation.

catalyst_text: Reached events triggering final analysis topline this quarter
detailed_catalyst_text: A pivotal Phase 3 trial in acute myeloid leukemia reached the pre-specified 80th death event, triggering the final analysis. The study evaluates maintenance therapy in patients in second complete remission. This milestone moves the program to database lock, unblinding, and statistical analysis of the primary endpoint.
catalyst_text_evidence: the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial evaluating galinpepimut-S (GPS) in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) has reached the pre-specified 80th event (number of deaths), triggering the final analysis of the study. The REGAL trial is an event-driven overall survival study, and with the occurrence of the 80th event, SELLAS will proceed with database lock, unblinding of the study data, and statistical analysis of the primary endpoint data.

catalyst_text: Reported survival events update final analysis at 80th
detailed_catalyst_text: An update from the Phase 3 REGAL overall survival trial in acute myeloid leukemia reported that 72 events had occurred as of 2025-12-26, short of the 80 events required to trigger the final analysis. The study remains blinded and the final analysis will be initiated once the 80th event occurs, clarifying current trial progress and timing.
catalyst_text_evidence: “SELLAS was informed by its contract research organization managing the REGAL trial that the pooled number of events was 72 as of 2025-12-26.” “SELLAS remains blinded to all efficacy and survival data outcomes and, as no outcomes analyses were performed and no statistical penalty has been incurred, this one-time update on the aggregate number of events does not impact future statistical analyses.” “Because the final analysis is event-driven, and the timing of studies with overall survival as an endpoint can vary, SELLAS will announce the 80th event when it occurs.”

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 2 data at hematology conference
detailed_catalyst_text: New Phase 2 data for a CDK9 inhibitor combined with azacitidine and venetoclax were presented for relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia with myelodysplastic syndrome-related changes after prior venetoclax therapy. Results showed a 46% overall response rate across cohorts, with 58% in patients with one prior line, and no dose-limiting toxicities observed. These findings indicate meaningful activity and tolerability in a heavily pretreated population, supporting continued development.
catalyst_text_evidence: SELLAS Life Sciences Group, Inc. ... today announced that clinical data from its ongoing Phase 2 study of SLS009, a highly selective CDK9 inhibitor, in combination with azacitidine (AZA) and venetoclax (VEN) ... were presented today at the 67th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting and Exposition, being held 2025-12-06 – 2025-12-09, in Orlando, Florida. SLS009 in combination with AZA/VEN demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in patients with R/R AML-MR, and among the 35 evaluable patients, the overall response rate (CR+CRi+MLFS) was 46%, including 29% achieving CR/CRi. Across all cohorts, patients with one prior line of therapy experienced the greatest benefit, with a 58% response rate and mOS not yet reached. No dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) or treatment-related deaths were observed, and the combination was well tolerated.
